coverage.note: This feed's first run. Three San Francisco articles queued and all three carry a street address and a building story; the two the screen skipped were a San Jose meeting notice and a Sacramento church site, both named as such in their headlines. Every item's first <category> is the address itself, so the addresses here were confirmed against the article text rather than found in it.

findings.description: Initial permits filed for a 40-storey, 433-foot mixed-use tower of 288 apartments on what is now a surface parking lot at the corner of 8th and Stevenson, in Mid-Market. Thirty-eight of the units would be affordable, split between low- and moderate-income households, and the application invokes SB 330 and the State Density Bonus law to raise capacity and streamline approval. Manna Capital is the developer and Handel Architects the designer. The property owner is a private family trust and is not recorded here.

citation.label: San Francisco YIMBY, “40-Story Skyscraper Proposed Near Civic Center, San Francisco,” 25 August 2026

findings.description: The affordable housing building at 730 Stanyan Street, on the former Haight Street McDonald's site, is open; all 160 units were leased before it opened and the ground-floor early childcare centre is near completion. OMA led the design with Y.A. Studio as executive architect, GLS on landscape and the Chinatown Community Development Center as sponsor. The facade is modular glass-fibre-reinforced concrete panels with integrated windows and louvres, and the southeast corner is carved back from the lot line to meet the neighbouring Victorian at 1760–1762 Waller Street. The date is the article's; the story says the building is already open and gives no opening date.

findings.description: Permits filed to convert an existing industrial building on a 0.18-acre lot between Folsom and Howard into a performing arts space: a 133-seat theatre with a double-height ceiling, a gallery at the lobby entrance, a meeting room and a restroom across the ground floor and mezzanine. The exterior is not to be altered and the second floor stays in office use. A partnership of the Asian Pacific Islander Cultural Center and Kularts leads the project, with Pyatok Architects designing; both are contributing institutions to the city's SOMA Pilipinas cultural district. Cost and timeline were not reported.
